seo.title: Frequently asked questions
seo.description: Answers about TablePro’s apps, supported databases, paid plans, licenses, privacy and accounts.

header.title: Frequently asked questions
header.lead: Questions about the apps, licenses and privacy.

items.question: What is TablePro?
answer: A native, open-source database client. On the Mac, query and edit {featuredEngines} and more, and work with schemas. The iPhone and iPad app offers a smaller set of database tools.
See all <features>features</features>.

items.question: What does “native” mean here?
answer: TablePro uses native interfaces and database drivers, without Electron or JDBC. The current apps use Swift: AppKit and SwiftUI on the Mac, and device features such as Face ID and Shortcuts on iPhone and iPad.

items.question: Is TablePro free?
answer: Yes. The Mac app has no trial period or time limit. All supported engines, AI, MCP and Safe Mode are free. Starter and Team add the features on the <pricing>pricing page</pricing>.
The iPhone and iPad app is free, with no license or in-app purchases.

items.question: Is TablePro open source?
answer: Yes. Both apps, including paid-feature code, are under the AGPLv3 in one <source>GitHub repository</source>. Builds from source still check licenses for paid features.

items.question: Can I use TablePro at work?
answer: Yes, in a company of any size. The AGPL places no conditions on running TablePro. They apply to distributing it, and to offering a modified version to others over a network. The <agpl>license text</agpl> has the details.

items.question: Which Macs does TablePro run on?
answer: The Mac app requires {macRequirement} and runs natively on Apple silicon and Intel. Get it from the <download>download page</download> or with Homebrew.

items.question: Is there an app for iPhone and iPad?
answer: Yes. The free App Store app requires {iosRequirement} and connects to {iosEngines}. It supports queries, SSH tunnels, Safe Mode and Face ID; table browsing and editing depend on the engine.
It has no AI assistant, MCP server or saved queries. See its <ios>features and limits</ios>.

items.question: Is there a version for Windows or Linux?
answer: No. There is no Windows version. A Linux prototype exists, but there is nothing to install and no release date.

items.question: Which languages are the apps in?
answer: The Mac app supports {macLanguages}, though some translated screens still show English. The iPhone and iPad app supports {iosLanguages}.
The website and account portal support multiple languages. <docs>Documentation</docs> is in English.

items.question: Which databases can I connect to?
answer: The Mac app supports {featuredEngines} and more. See <databases>supported databases</databases> for each engine’s capabilities.
The iPhone and iPad app connects to {iosEngines}.

items.question: Do I have to install database drivers?
answer: Drivers for {bundledEngines} are bundled on the Mac. Others download on first use, require internet access and update independently. TablePro verifies their checksum and code signature.
All iPhone and iPad drivers are built in.

items.question: Can I connect through SSH or TLS?
answer: Yes, where the engine supports them. The Mac app supports SSH keys, passwords, agents and jump hosts, plus TLS certificate verification and external tunnels or proxies. See <connections>connection options</connections>.
On iPhone and iPad, SSH uses a password or private key. Jump hosts are not supported.

items.question: Where are my passwords stored?
answer: Saved passwords stay in the Keychain. On the Mac, you can instead resolve them from files, environment variables, shell commands, 1Password, Vault or AWS Secrets Manager.
Password sync is a separate opt-in: enable <ui>Passwords</ui> on the Mac or <ui>Sync Passwords</ui> on iPhone and iPad. It uses iCloud Keychain.

items.question: Can I bring my connections from another app?
answer: Yes. The Mac app imports connections and saved passwords from {importApps}. Importing is free.

items.question: What does a license add?
answer: Starter adds {starterFeatures} to the Mac app. Team also adds {teamFeatures}. See <pricing>paid features</pricing> for details.

items.question: How much does a license cost?
answer: Choose monthly, yearly or one-time billing in US dollars. Team starts at {teamMinSeats} seats. See current <pricing>prices and totals</pricing>.

items.question: How many Macs does a license cover?
answer: Starter covers one person on up to {deviceLimit} Macs. Team has at least {teamMinSeats} seats, and each seat covers one person on up to {deviceLimit} Macs. The limit is per account, across Starter and Team. iPhone and iPad use no seat.
To use your license on another Mac, remove one in <ui>Settings > Account</ui> or on the Devices page in <account>your account</account>. Until then, the other Mac keeps the free features.

items.question: What happens when my subscription ends?
answer: Paid features stop: iCloud Sync pauses and shared connections may be hidden. Your local connections, queries and settings remain. Free features keep working; renewing restores paid access.
One-time licenses have no expiry date. iPhone and iPad are unaffected.

items.question: Does a license work offline?
answer: Yes. TablePro keeps a signed copy of your plan and renews it when it starts and once a day. If our server cannot be reached, paid features keep working until that copy expires, at most {offlineDays} days after the last renewal.

For a Mac that never goes online, create an offline file in <account>your account</account> and import it in <ui>Settings > Account</ui>. It lasts until the end of the paid period, or a year for a one-time purchase.
Versions before TablePro accounts check the license every {revalidateDays} days instead, and keep paid features for {graceDays} days after the last successful check.
Driver downloads, updates and cloud AI still need internet access.

items.question: Who handles the payment?
answer: {merchant} is the merchant of record and handles payment, tax and receipts. Your card and invoices are in <portal>{merchant}’s customer portal</portal>, which you sign in to with your purchase email. Change or cancel a subscription in <account>your account</account>.

items.question: Which payment methods can I use?
answer: {merchant}’s checkout takes credit and debit cards.

items.question: Can I get an invoice for my company?
answer: Yes. In <portal>{merchant}’s customer portal</portal> you can add a company name, a VAT number and a billing address to an invoice, then download it.

items.question: Can I get a refund?
answer: Yes. Purchases and subscription renewals are refundable within {refundDays} days of each charge. Refund one yourself in Billing in <account>your account</account>, or see the <refundPolicy>refund policy</refundPolicy>.

items.question: I lost my license key. Where is it?
answer: You no longer need it. Sign in to the Mac app with the email you bought with: your purchase is in that account. Updating TablePro signs you in with a key already on your Mac.
Only versions before TablePro accounts still ask for the key, which is in your purchase email. Purchases made since then come without one.

items.question: What is priority support?
answer: It comes with a Team license: emails from Team customers are answered first, within one business day. The <termsSupport>terms</termsSupport> describe support for every plan.

items.question: What do the apps send to TablePro?
answer: The Mac app sends a daily usage report by default; disable it in <ui>Settings > General > Privacy</ui>. It includes a hashed machine ID, app details and database types, never hostnames, usernames, passwords, queries or rows.

Once you sign in, the Mac app registers your Mac with your account, sending its machine ID, name and app and macOS versions, and renews your plan once a day. Versions before TablePro accounts send the license key with those details every {revalidateDays} days. iPhone and iPad reports are opt-in. Team Library receives settings and saved SQL you publish. See the <privacy>privacy policy</privacy>, including IP logging.

items.question: Do I need to sign up?
answer: No sign-up is needed to use the apps. Paid features work once you sign in to a TablePro account: a purchase goes to the account of the email you bought with, created if there is none, and each team member signs in with their own. Versions before TablePro accounts take a license key instead.

items.question: Does the AI assistant send my data to TablePro?
answer: No. Requests go directly to your chosen provider, not through TablePro. They include the database type and name, schema and current query by default. Result rows need a separate opt-in. {localAiProviders} run locally. Providers may charge for use. See <aiMcp>AI data handling</aiMcp>.

items.question: What does iCloud Sync store, and where?
answer: Sync is off by default and uses a private database in your iCloud account, which TablePro cannot read. Passwords require a separate opt-in: <ui>Passwords</ui> on the Mac or <ui>Sync Passwords</ui> on iPhone and iPad.
iCloud Sync requires Starter or Team on the Mac and is free on iPhone and iPad.

items.question: How do I sign in to my account?
answer: In <account>your account</account>, enter your email to get a sign-in link and a 6-digit code, or use a passkey, Apple, GitHub or Google. There is no password. The link works once, and both expire after 15 minutes.

The Mac app offers to sign you in when it first starts, and later in <ui>Settings > Account</ui>. It opens the sign-in page in a browser sheet, where you type the code from the email. Versions before TablePro accounts have no sign-in.

items.question: How do I add or remove team members?
answer: Owners and admins invite people by email from the Members page in <account>your account</account>, with a role and, if they choose, a seat. The emailed link works for 7 days, and any TablePro account can accept it. New members use their seat in the version of TablePro that adds accounts.
Removing a member frees their seat. Their Macs lose Team’s features the next time TablePro checks in.

items.question: How do I change the number of seats?
answer: The team’s owner changes seats in Billing in <account>your account</account>. For a subscription, {merchant} charges or credits the prorated difference at once. A team without a subscription buys more one-time seats there.

items.question: How do I cancel a subscription?
answer: Cancel in <account>your account</account> or <portal>{merchant}’s portal</portal>. Access continues through the paid period without another renewal. You can resume before it ends.

items.question: Do I have to set up my connections again?
answer: If your current client is supported, you can import connections from {importApps}, including saved passwords, SSH tunnels and TLS settings.

items.question: How does TablePro compare with other database clients?
answer: See <compare>comparisons</compare> for differences, checked dates and sources, including where another client may fit better.
